items.title: Show HN: Navital Gym – open environments for testing AI agents on Indian tasks
items.story_key: story|title:navital gym open environments for testing ai agents on indian tasks
items.content_excerpt: Deterministic, auto-graded environments for AI agents on Indian-reality tasks: UPI, GST, trip planning, forms, Hindi/Hinglish support. Rule-based grading, no LLM judge. Deterministic, auto-graded environments for AI agents doing tasks set in India: planning a trip around rail quotas and waitlists, GST invoicing, filling forms, answering customers in Hindi and other Indian languages. By Navital Labs . Navital Gym is public and in active development: results are added as runs finish (see docs/RESULTS.md). Read this first. Every environment uses a simplified, documented version of Indian practice and synthetic data . These are tests for AI agents, not statements about current law, railway, bank or tax rules. Not affiliated with or endorsed by NPCI, RBI, GSTN / CBIC, IRCTC / Indian Railways, any bank or any government body; names are used only to describe the workflow. Not financial or tax advice. Each env README states its own rules and an "as of" date. Every env README carries its simplified rules and the sources of any real-world figure. Run any model that speaks the OpenAI chat API with tool calling (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio, hosted): --agent "openai:qwen2.5:7b@http://localhost:11434/v1" (the key is read from the provider's environment variable, OPENAI_API_KEY for openai: specs including a custom @base_url , GROQ_API_KEY , GEMINI_API_KEY , ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ; never from the command line). Reports show pass@1, pass^k, per-rule failures, and separate tables per split (core / experimental) and kind (feasible / infeasible), so one mixed number is never the headline. Pass@1 on deterministic stratified samples or whole splits (k=1, one run per cell; n = tasks, so one task is 1/n of the cell: read small-n cells as indicative). 'easy' columns are the easy tier (designed so a 7B-30B model can sometimes solve them); the others are the standard tasks. Full tables with format failures, strict (no-repair) pass@1, partial credit, spend, dates and commits: docs/RESULTS.md . Every row was re-graded by the same grading code ( scripts/regrade.py ); check it with git rev-parse v1.0.1:navital_gym (see docs/RESULTS.md ). Small and mid-size models: partial credit (mean fraction of scored rules passed; shows progress where pass@1 is near zero) Most of the models people will test are small or mid-size, so they come first. items.title: DoorDash Cuts Grocery Reorder Latency from 16 to 2 Seconds with AI Agents
items.summary:
DoorDash reduced grocery reorder latency from 16 to 2 seconds by precomputing recurring purchase needs using batch LLM inference and deterministic validation. Live catalog resolution keeps product selections current, while an editable shopping interface avoids unnecessary model calls. The company reports that shopping list views doubled and the flow’s order rate increased by approximately 34%

By Leela Kumili

items.title: Show HN: SpecDeck – Bring coding agent decisions back into the spec
items.summary: Writing good specs is hard. You don’t know everything upfront and it’s impossible to write every little detail in the spec. Much of my job as a developer has been to treat specs as intent, and fill out the blanks in the code and use the code reviews as a way to question those decisions. But as coding agents have started to produce much more code, the decisions that actually affect the product are getting harder to find. So I created SpecDeck. It helps everyone on the team write specs and hand them over to developers and their agents through MCP. During implementation, agents write the decisions that matter back as proposed spec changes and leave smaller implementation choices in the code. When the work is done, a person reviews and publish those changes into the spec. The workflow is modeled on git: a published spec is main, drafts are branches, and proposals are pull requests. It should feel familiar to developers, while making it easy for the whole team to work with specs and keep them up to date without touching git. It’s still early and there’s plenty to improve, but I’d love to hear your feedback.

items.content_excerpt: A longitudinal archive of AI chatbot responses: a curated, evolving set of questions is put to a wide range of AI models every day, and the responses are recorded so you can compare how models respond and see how those responses change over time. Query Questions, Models, and Responses over HTTP or bulk export daily data, plus a machine-readable OpenAPI schema. items.title: Preserving Utility in Continual LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Projections
items.summary: Unlearning concerns the task of removing the influence of a sensitive portion of the training data, such as protected, copyrighted or private text, from a model without retraining it from scratch. While unlearning requests happen continuously during a model's lifetime, the vast majority of LLM unlearning methods are ill-suited for iterated removal, yielding steep decay in forgetting and utility upon sequential unlearning. This decay stems from interference between successive updates, as each new deletion can undo earlier ones or push the model further along directions already degraded by them. To address this, we introduce Continual Orthogonal Projection (COP), a gradient-projection scheme that restricts each update to the orthogonal complement of activation subspaces cached from prior forget sets. This approach provably guarantees first-order non-interference with earlier deletions. COP stores only a low-rank basis per layer, requiring neither past gradients nor previous forget sets, and plugs into unlearning methods that update the model through gradient steps on a differentiable loss without modifying its objective. Experiments on standard LLM unlearning benchmarks (TOFU and RWKU) show that COP preserves utility across sequential requests without weakening forgetting, preventing the collapse of standard objectives and forgetting more effectively than continual-specific baselines.

items.title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation commonly serves separate models for reranking and answering, duplicating model residency and passage processing. We introduce Glance, which equips the generator with a lightweight decision adapter and pointer head to score candidate passages from a shared prefill. Short relevance probes branch from the cached context, producing one score per passage without separately prefilling each query-passage pair. A single resident 9B backbone supports generation, general decisions and reranking, with approximately 0.1 GiB of additional memory per decision skill. After 39 minutes of MS MARCO fine-tuning, Glance achieves nDCG@10 of 0.741 on SciFact and 0.345 on NFCorpus, compared with 0.721 and 0.326 for bge-reranker-v2-m3. On 300 HotpotQA questions, its selected context improves answer F1 by 0.045 over cross-encoder-selected context under the same base generator (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.014, 0.076]). In a scaling study, reranking quality keeps rising up to 200 candidates (43k tokens) scored from one shared prefill, where it exceeds the cross-encoder by 0.058 nDCG@10, and a probe-only activated adapter lets generation continue from the original passage cache. These initial results demonstrate generator-based reranking with one resident backbone; evaluation currently covers two retrieval datasets, one QA dataset and one backbone family.

items.title: Does Federated Training Degrade Explainability? A Comparative Analysis of Grad-CAM Faithfulness in Centralized vs. Federated Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Automated detection has become the essential safeguard against realistic synthetic media, but deploying it at scale requires training on sensitive data from multiple organizations, putting privacy and the transparency demanded by forensic review in direct conflict. Federated learning resolves the privacy side by sharing only model updates rather than raw data, but whether this comes at the cost of trustworthy gradient-based explanations, which analysts rely on to decide whether or not to trust a flagged clip, has not been studied. We present the systematic study of Grad-CAM explanation faithfulness under federated deepfake detection, evaluating an EfficientNet-B4 detector on FaceForensics++ across five federated clients under varying degrees of data heterogeneity. We find that the relationship between federation and explanation quality is non-monotonic: at near-IID (Independent and Identically Distributed Data) and moderate heterogeneity, federated models match or exceed the faithfulness of a centralized baseline, but at extreme heterogeneity, explanations break down entirely, becoming spatially incoherent and, on average, causally misleading. This degradation is not a general cost of federated training but a threshold effect tied to client heterogeneity, and we offer practical guidance for identifying when privacy-preserving deepfake detection can be deployed safely and when its explanations can no longer be trusted. Code and data partitions are available for reproducibility.

items.title: Serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at Scale: vLLM Matches DeepInfer and Scales to GB300 NVL72
items.summary: With P/D disaggregation and Wide-EP on a GB300 NVL72 rack, vLLM serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on SemiAnalysis AgentX at 954K tokens/s per GPU at a P90 of 196 tokens/s per user, 7.9x our aggregated single-node result.
items.story_key: model:deepseek|ver:4.1|variant:flash|title:serving deepseek v4 1 flash at scale vllm matches deepinfer and scales to gb300

A specialized decode path reaches 826 tokens/s for a single user. Against DeepInfer, DeepSeek's own engine, vLLM's decode throughput is within 6% across batch sizes 8–256, and its prefill tracks DeepInfer's published curve. The efficiency comes from deliberate engineering on components that vLLM already has, built on the kernels DeepSeek open-sourced. This post walks through our performance study, breaks down each optimization, and shares the lessons we learned: Figure 1: SemiAnalysis AgentX on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72: vLLM with P/D disaggregation and Wide-EP (gold) achieves a further 7.9× throughput increase over our aggregated single-node result from the first post . Throughput counts cached input, uncached input and output tokens ( source ). DeepInfer is DeepSeek's own inference engine for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, released this week as an offline engine with published prefill and decode curves. It is the most relevant reference for this model, so before going into our optimizations we show where vLLM stands against it. Decode. Under DeepSeek's decode configuration (131K context, nextn=3), vLLM on GB200 achieves throughput within 6% of DeepInfer's published results across batch sizes 8 to 256 (Figure 2). Figure 2: Decode output throughput per GPU vs. batch size at 131K context, nextn=3. vLLM on GB200 vs. DeepInfer's published results, read from the charts in its README ( source ). Prefill. DeepInfer's published prefill curve uses EP4DP4 with 32 redundant experts and a 140-token bounded replay, on hardware the chart does not state, and we read its values off the chart. Our run uses DEP2 on GB300 with no redundant experts, a 128-token replay and our own prompts. Because the setups differ, we do not read the gap between the two curves as an engine-to-engine speedup. What Figure 3 shows is that vLLM's DEP2 prefill tracks DeepSeek's own engine across the range they published. items.title: Understanding and Mitigating Role Spoofing in LLMs
items.summary: Despite growing capabilities, LLMs remain susceptible to prompt injections: malicious inputs that can manipulate or hijack models. In particular, it has recently been observed that LLMs can exhibit role confusion (Ye et al., 2026), where models attribute the source of text based on its style instead of its labeled role. Malicious text in tool outputs (for instance, a malicious webpage accessed by an agent) can leverage role confusion to impersonate the user, an attack we call role spoofing}. In this work, we seek to understand and mitigate role spoofing. We study how models track "who said what" in a conversation, showing that they use cues from both content (e.g., semantics and writing style) and structure (e.g., control tokens and formatting). We show that LLMs are highly susceptible to role spoofing attacks that combine both fake structure and content. Additionally, in a toy setting, we show that adversarial training which teaches the model to ignore content-based injections does mitigate content-based attacks but leaves the model susceptible to structure-based attacks. This can explain why frontier models, with increased resistance to many injection attacks, can still be susceptible to role spoofing. Finally, we propose a new method for detecting role spoofing using linear probes trained to predict roles in a conversation, and show that it is effective across different settings.

items.title: claude-code v2.1.311
items.summary:
What's changed

  • Added --hold-idle-file and --max-hold-min to self-hosted-runner, to keep an idle session while your host reports processes it left running
  • Added a tip for the Explanatory output style, shown when you ask Claude for explanations
  • Fixed long freezes at startup and after reading or editing files when a CLAUDE.md file holds a very long list item
  • Fixed interrupting Claude not taking effect until a timeout while an MCP server had not answered a resource read or a skill was still downloading
  • Fixed standard-context sessions stopping with "Usage credits required for 1M context" when a request ran over 200K tokens; Claude Code now compacts the conversation and continues
  • Fixed Write and Edit stalling for up to 5 seconds after they ran, and reporting 0 lines changed, when changing thousands of lines in a file
  • Fixed subagents being unable to use MCP tools from servers that finish connecting after the subagent starts
  • Fixed Claude seeing stale MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md content right after automatic compaction when those files were edited earlier in the session
  • Fixed claude -p and SDK sessions saving transcript messages out of order or keeping messages that were taken back
  • Fixed SubagentStop hooks running about twice a minute for each running subagent instead of once when it finishes
  • Fixed the @ file picker ignoring .ignore/.rgignore negation rules that re-include git-ignored files
  • Fixed a subagent's isolated worktree being removed while a background subagent it started was still working in it
  • Fixed background agents in auto mode that wait on their own shells starting a new main conversation turn on every wake
  • Fixed the Bash tool description claiming the working directory always persists between calls
  • Fixed the environment block naming a shell commands don't run in, such as fish when the Bash tool uses zsh
  • Fixed claude mcp add, claude mcp remove and /mcp naming the current folder instead of the project entry in ~/.claude.json that holds a local-scope server when run below a repository root
  • Fixed claude mcp list and claude mcp get showing the error code twice on failed-connection lines (for example ENOENT: ENOENT: …)
  • Fixed Remote Control sessions staying on "Connecting" for about two minutes when a network proxy blocks a startup request
  • Fixed messages that Claude sends to a cloud or Remote Control session appearing as your own message in the Claude mobile apps
  • Fixed Claude not being told the cause when a file attached to a message sent over Remote Control or to a cloud session could not be saved because the disk was full, or that a message's attachments past the first 20 were left out
  • Fixed WebFetch and WebSearch hanging on a stalled response in Cowork cloud sessions; an unfinished request now fails after 300 seconds
  • Fixed a background session that crashed between turns not being restarted while it was attached, pinned, or had a scheduled task or wake-up set
  • Fixed the "background service did not respond" error suggesting the disabled claude daemon restart; it now suggests claude daemon stop --any and says it ends background sessions
  • Fixed claude respawn <id> starting the background service before reporting that no background session matches the id
  • Fixed /effort not warning about a prompt cache miss in plan mode when the plan model differs from the session model
  • Fixed /ide saying the VS Code extension was installed before the install finished or when it failed
  • Fixed the Write tool's file preview skipping rows and miscounting hidden lines when a line is wider than the terminal
  • Fixed ↑ in an agent's chat tab recalling a message that was still waiting to be delivered, so resending it sent a second copy
  • Fixed Cowork cloud sessions losing their connectors and most tools after a restart when a plugin or your settings named an agent; Cowork cloud sessions now ignore that setting
  • Fixed agent teams sessions showing an empty task list when coming back with --resume, --continue, /resume or --session-id, including after /clear or a crash, and /branch writing to the original session's list
  • Fixed pasting text that mentions an image file, such as ! open /tmp/shot.png or /review look at /tmp/shot.png, attaching the image and dropping its path from the prompt
  • Fixed the feedback draft card showing its 1/2/0 and Esc shortcuts while the prompt has text, when those keys act on the prompt instead of the card
  • Fixed a lone backslash in quotes or brackets, like "\" or (\), disappearing from Claude's responses
  • Fixed agent teammates compacting their history when DISABLE_COMPACT is set
  • Fixed the rewind menu offering "Summarize from here" and "Summarize up to here" when DISABLE_COMPACT is set
  • Fixed a finished /code-review, or another skill that runs in a sub-agent, running a second time when a cloud or background session restarts
  • Fixed long hidden thinking being cut off as idle on Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS, where the endpoint sends thinking progress updates
  • Fixed /ide saying it had installed the JetBrains plugin when nothing was installed
  • Fixed Claude Pro and Max subscribers being told to ask their admin when their subscription can't be used; the message now points to billing settings
  • Fixed the diff pane opening by itself after an edit in wide fullscreen terminals when it had nothing to show
  • Fixed /mcp showing a remote server as failed after "Clear authentication" when the server works without sign-in
  • Fixed /mcp showing "authenticated" for a remote server that Claude Code sends no credentials to
  • Fixed a --plugin-dir folder of plugins loading as one plugin when an empty .mcp.json was at its top
  • Fixed /usage never showing large prompt-cache misses under "What's contributing to your limits usage?"
  • Fixed status line links staying plain text in background sessions after you open them from a terminal that supports links
  • Fixed the /rewind confirmation saying the conversation "will be forked" when the later messages are removed from the conversation
  • Fixed the /rewind warning that wrongly said manual and Bash edits are never affected by a code restore
  • Fixed plan approval in screen reader mode sending feedback you had dismissed with Escape
  • Fixed Claude Code retrying requests the API marked not to retry, which could hold a turn for minutes or, in unattended retry mode (CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG), indefinitely
  • Linux: Fixed sandboxed Bash commands failing with bwrap: Can't create file when a --plugin-dir folder was also an added directory and permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories was on
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed a session failing to start when a rate limit (HTTP 429, or a git wrapper that exits 75) blocks an added read-only repository; it now starts without that repository
  • Improved startup time for Pro and Max accounts by skipping two network requests on launches within an hour of the last check
  • Improved /teleport and claude --teleport to warn when a compacted cloud session loads from its last compaction, so the messages it summarized aren't in the local copy
  • Improved the messages shown when a background session's process exits: they no longer promise a restart that isn't coming, and they say how to resume the session
  • Improved artifacts with several views: Claude now routes each view on the link's #name and no longer says the address bar stays the same as you switch views
  • Improved shell commands that reach their timeout: the result now shows the output so far and says the command is still running in the background
  • Improved compaction: when the model's reply has no summary in it, Claude Code now usually asks for the summary once more before it replaces the conversation
  • Improved the Artifact tool's choice between a page and a document: explainers and visual or interactive work become artifact pages; documents are for writing people keep editing or pass around
  • Improved startup time for launches whose only arguments are options and their values, such as claude --model opus
  • Improved the "Connection dropped" API error: it now says where to look first (the proxy or gateway in use, else VPN or firewall; Anthropic API only, Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry are unchanged)
  • Improved screen reader mode: deleting a rule in /permissions says "Deleted allow rule …" right away
  • Improved the message shown when a pasted sign-in code is refused: it now says the code may have expired or been used, and to sign in again
  • Improved Slack connector sends: Claude now checks a channel's topic for posting rules before messaging a channel you didn't name
  • Improved screen reader mode: Claude's questions are listed as "Questions: Color (answered), Pages", without arrows or symbols
  • Changed ultrathink in the interactive terminal to run its turn at xhigh effort on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1 through Anthropic's API; typed while Claude is working, it raises the rest of that turn
  • Changed the ultrathink rainbow to appear only where the keyword can raise effort, and not when the word is quoted or part of a file path
  • Changed Ctrl+D in agent view to match the prompt: on an empty input, pressing it twice exits
  • Changed --output-format json and stream-json output to write DEL, C1 control and Unicode format characters inside strings as \uXXXX escapes; parsed values are unchanged
  • Changed model names and IDs to drop the [1m] suffix and its label on models where the suffix has no effect; the suffix is still accepted
  • Changed startup warnings about permission rules in settings files to show once per user until the rule changes
  • Changed /code-review to tell Claude to put the effort level first and use max only when asked
  • Changed DISABLE_COMPACT in settings files and in a mod's $.env.set so they can only turn compaction off, not back on
  • Changed Claude Code on Bedrock, Mantle, Vertex, and Foundry to load model settings from a signed file on downloads.claude.ai; set CLAUDE_CODE_MODEL_CATALOG=off to turn this off
  • Changed sessions that set CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS with feature-flag fetching off to reuse a claude.ai skills list up to 10 minutes old that another session on the machine fetched
  • Changed clicks on scrollbar arrows and bars in fullscreen lists to act when the mouse button is released, so moving off the scrollbar before letting go cancels the click
  • Changed claude purge to say it deletes data only on this computer, not anything stored by Anthropic
  • [VSCode] Added syntax coloring to code blocks in Claude's replies, in light, dark and high contrast dark themes
  • [VSCode] Added a "Running UserPromptSubmit hooks" spinner status and screen reader announcement for slow UserPromptSubmit hooks
  • [VSCode] Fixed custom skills and custom slash commands sent from the VS Code or JetBrains panel leaving out the open file or selected lines that ordinary messages include (#102799)
  • [VSCode] Fixed the extension host freezing while the login shell ran its start-up files to read PATH on macOS and Linux
  • [VSCode] Fixed clicking an image in a tool result, or closing its preview, also opening the result's text in an editor tab
  • [VSCode] Fixed voice dictation continuing to record after a message was sent with the Send button; sending now stops dictation first, as pressing Enter already did
  • [VSCode] Changed the extension to start Claude Code sessions with DISABLE_TELEMETRY set while VS Code's telemetry setting is off, so they send no usage metrics or error reports and fetch no feature flags
  • [VSCode] Changed the session list side bar to load Web sessions when the Web tab is first opened, not at startup
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed routines in Anthropic-hosted environments staying locked after their owner left the organization and rejoined; the owner can now turn them back on
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed a failed routine API token delete or regenerate showing nothing if the edit dialog had already closed; it now shows an error toast
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed cloud environment dialogs, including the admin dialog, accepting duplicate names; they now refuse a name another listed environment already has
  • [Claude Tag] Added a Skills view to Claude Tag analytics showing how often Claude runs each attached skill in Slack channels and which go unused, with Usage links in admin settings
  • [Claude Tag] Improved Claude Tag routines that run in a new session: a run with nothing to report can now end without posting a throwaway message to the channel
  • [Claude Tag] Changed Claude Tag admin settings to show a lock instead of # for private Slack channels that your own Slack account can see
  • [Code Review] Improved Code Review's check run to say no further automatic review will start when the model still can't analyze a change on the automatic retry
  • [Code Review] Improved Code Review reliability: a review whose session fails to start because of a transient server fault is now retried once automatically, and its check run says so
